thread:
Alex C: FYI escalated ticket from DocuCorp — they say streaming responses are much slower since yesterday. p95 TTFB up from ~120ms to ~700-900ms for streaming endpoints. non-stream total time looks similar or a bit better. ticket: #2457 :eyes:
Maria P: Can you drop repro steps + request IDs? also link to the metric dashboard if you have it so SRE can see p95/p99 trends?
Alex C: Repro steps below. request ids: r-8f3a2c and r-8f3a9f. dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/streams?env=prod&range=1h (private link)
Alex C: curl test (streaming):
```
curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=rw-large&stream=true
```
Response: headers arrive fast, but first data chunk comes ~800ms after headers. then small bursts.
Alex C: same request with stream=false returns whole payload in ~600ms (total), so puzzling: streaming TTFB > non-stream total.
Kevin H: That pattern usually means buffering between runtime and client. Could be LB/proxy (CloudFront/NGINX/Envoy) or gzip/transfer-encoding behavior. Do we know if this customer routes through a CDN?
Alex C: They use CloudFront in front of our API (standard).
Jordan (oncall): Likely culprit: CloudFront + compression + small chunk sizes = CloudFront waits to coalesce before forwarding. Also check nginx proxy_buffering and envoy's http2 settings.
Maria P: Can you try two things: 1) bypass CDN (direct to origin) and 2) curl with --no-buffer and --raw to ensure client isn't buffering? Also capture tcpdump for the r-8f3a2c request so we can see chunk timing.
Alex C: Ran quick bypass test (direct origin): TTFB drops to ~130ms. So confirms CDN/proxy layer.
Kevin H: That confirms it. Root cause candidate: CloudFront is re-chunking/rewriting responses and coalescing small writes. Runtime was emitting tiny chunks (8–64 bytes) with infrequent flush. When non-streaming we buffer server-side and send single bigger response so total is lower. Need to adjust flush cadence or enable chunked streaming passthrough at the CDN.
Jordan (oncall): Short-term mitigation for DocuCorp: route them to dedicated origin (bypass CF) or ask them to use non-streaming endpoint (stream=false) while we investigate. Also we can enable a config flag to increase server-side chunk sizes / flush more aggressively for that customer.
Kevin H: Dev notes for runtime changes: check our flush interval (currently 200ms or when buffer > 1KB). If we're holding <200ms for small tokens it might explain the delay. Options: reduce flush interval to 50ms for streaming or accumulate to 2KB before flush. Also consider sending periodic keepalive/chunk heartbeats so proxies forward earlier.
Maria P: For CloudFront: confirm if Response Compression is enabled; gzip can cause CF to buffer until threshold. Also check CF's "Minimum TTL" and origin response buffering. We need a ticket with edge config team if it's CF-managed.
Alex C: Customer said they didn't change their side. This started after our runtime rollout an hour earlier (rollout id r-2026-03-15-rtg2). Could be server side change.
Kevin H: Rollout note: we changed the streaming writer to emit smaller immediate token deltas and rely on nginx to flush. That exposes proxy buffering bugs. Reverting to prior flush behavior is an option.
Jordan (oncall): Action list:
- Alex: ask customer to test direct origin + provide tcpdump (done for quick test).
- Kevin: revert streaming writer change on a canary or add feature flag to use old flush behavior. (P0 for affected customers)
- Maria: open CF edge ticket and ask CDN team to confirm chunking passthrough; also check envoy/nginx buffering config on origin.
- SRE: add synthetic tests for streaming TTFB (measure header vs first byte across regions).
Alex C: I've offered DocuCorp the non-streaming fallback and also a temporary origin bypass. They're OK with fallback for now.
Kevin H: Repro tips for devs: use `curl -i -N --no-buffer` and `python -c 'import sys,requests; print(requests.get(URL, stream=True).raw.read(1))'` to observe first-byte behavior. Also test with `nghttp` or `s_client` to check HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1 differences.
Maria P: If we can't change CF behavior quickly, prioritize runtime revert/flag. We should also push a quick change to emit a 1KB initial buffer on stream start to coerce proxies to forward.
Jordan (oncall): Marking this P1 for DocuCorp support (they're in prod). Assign eng-runtime (Kevin) and eng-infra (Maria). I'll create an incident channel and ping infra oncall. :rotating_light:
support-bot: Incident channel created: #incident-1767123456-streaming-ttfb.
Alex C: Adding customer's repro payload and headers to the incident. Also adding logs showing small flushes: `2026-03-15T10:23:11Z r-8f3a2c flushed 24B`, `2026-03-15T10:23:12Z r-8f3a2c flushed 12B`
Kevin H: Plan: 1) roll back the writer change to canary tonight, 2) add feature flag to control flush cadence, 3) add a streaming-heartbeat message every 100ms during long responses. Will update ticket with PR/rollout IDs.
Maria P: Postmortem triggers: verify p95/p99 impact across customers, track which CDNs are affected, and ensure synthetic checks catch this class of regression in future.
Alex C: Customer accepted fallback. I'll keep them updated and close support ticket once rollback or config fix is live. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Jordan (oncall): Good triage. Keep incident channel updated with timeline and rollback progress.
Kevin H: I'll post a follow-up with the canary rollout schedule.
Alex C: Closing loop here for now, moving conversation to #incident-1767123456-streaming-ttfb per bot.
